brief: Goldman frames the week as positioning ahead of three catalysts: 3Q earnings season, the next Fed meeting, and the Midterms. US 10-year yields are little changed WTD, still elevated at 5.25%, which GS attributes to a post-pandemic echo-boom inflation impulse from higher import tariffs and the US-Iran War's hit to oil and refined product supply. GS expects a second Fed hike in December but sees a strong chance the FOMC ultimately decides further tightening is unnecessary; if wrong and rates stay higher for longer, Mei estimates GDP drag could exceed 0.5pp. Separately, sovereign debt stress is emerging in Europe, notably France. On earnings, Snider expects most S&P 500 companies to beat, implying 27% yoy EPS growth, with focus on AI monetization; Ramsden's bank preview flags cautious optimism, a capital markets slowdown, strong NII, and moderating capital returns. Prediction markets moved further toward Democrats taking the Senate and imply over 90% odds of a House majority. Taiwan and Korea now account for half the MXAPJ weight on AI hardware strength, surpassing China.
